clue.text: A burden not laid upon the poor

definitions.text: A burden not laid upon the poor

parts.words: A burden not laid upon the poor
parts.note: a fiscal charge levied only on the rich, so by design the poor escape it

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a certain load is spared the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' suggests a physical load, but here it is a levy; the poor escape it because it falls only on large fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on accumulated riches is a fiscal burden that, by its nature, never falls on people without money.

clue.text: She's well and truly partial

indicators.note: partial says only part of the words is used, so the answer sits inside the run well and

explanation.surface: A woman described as thoroughly biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well and truly' reads as one idiom, but 'truly partial' is the signal that the answer is a part of 'well and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name stands for a female person, so the pronoun works as the definition.

clue.text: Real upset, upset, he was, on hearing of Ophelia's misfortunes

annotationWithheld.why: Real upset, upset, he was, on hearing of Ophelia's misfortunes (7): LAERTES needs anagram of REAL plus TES, which only comes from reading 'upset' as 'set' going up, so that word is both fodder and reversal indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Real upset, upset, he was, on hearing of Ophelia's misfortunes

clue.text: Nevertheless, we linger around

indicators.note: around tells us that the linger synonym is wrapped about the word we

parts.note: to linger in one spot is to hover

explanation.surface: Someone stays on regardless, dawdling near the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts HOVER (linger) round WE, which stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs of contrast meaning 'in spite of that'.

clue.text: Makes public displays of affectation?

definitions.meaning: to broadcast or voice something openly
putting on pretentious manners, as in 'giving oneself graces'

explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster puts a programme on the radio, a verb sense; a snob's pretentious mannerisms are the noun sense.

clue.text: A break in the snow clad mountains?

definitions.text: A break in the snow clad mountains?

parts.words: A break in the snow clad mountains?
parts.note: a break read as a vacation spent on wintry slopes rather than a gap or a fracture in the rock

explanation.surface: A gap or fracture appears high in snowy peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' suggests a crack in the mountain; it is a vacation taken on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacation spent on snowy slopes going downhill on runners is a break in the mountains.

clue.text: Nobody will work to make it a success

definitions.text: Nobody will work to make it a success

parts.words: Nobody will work to make it a success
parts.note: the venture succeeds only if every worker in the land downs tools

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction that no one will put in effort for a project.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like idleness dooming a project; a nationwide stoppage succeeds precisely when nobody works.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide walkout by all trades succeeds only when the whole workforce stays away from the job.

clue.text: Trained hand who is perfectly capable of getting a job done

definitions.text: Trained hand who is perfectly capable of getting a job done

parts.words: Trained hand who is perfectly capable of getting a job done
parts.note: hand in its sense of a labourer, here one with craft training and competence

explanation.surface: A description of a competent, experienced employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman with training and expertise is a hand competent at any task set.

clue.text: Just cut?

parts.note: just read as the adjective equitable and cut as a noun meaning portion, not as an adverb and a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just cut' reads as 'only sliced' or 'freshly trimmed'; read 'just' as equitable and 'cut' as a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: An equitable portion is a proper allocation of the proceeds that a person is entitled to.

clue.text: Get one playing snooker, maybe

parts.note: get one read as scoring a single point at the table, which happens when a crimson ball is sunk

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to score a point during a game of snooker.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker each red ball is worth one point, so sinking a red scores one. The grid's POTTIERED is a typo for this.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking a crimson ball at snooker scores a single point, so the phrase is one way to get one.

clue.text: A free description of much of Arizona

parts.note: to free someone of something is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: A liberal account of most of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A free' looks like an adjective phrase; it is A plus RID.
explanation.definitionFit: Most of Arizona is desert, so the adjective for very dry land describes it.

clue.text: Spoiled votes may be cast into one

definitions.text: Spoiled votes may be cast into one

indicators.note: spoiled marks the letters of votes as messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ballot papers ruined at an election end up melted down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled votes' are ballots defaced at an election; 'cast' hints at cast iron, the material of an old-fashioned heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen range or heater is often made of cast iron, so it is something metal is cast into.

clue.text: A tyrant in whose reign eroticism flourished

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run reign eroticism

explanation.surface: A despot whose rule saw debauchery thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the Roman emperor's notorious court, so the answer belongs in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor remembered for cruelty and persecution is a byword for despotism.

clue.text: Split I've discerned in the Senior Service

indicators.note: in places the word I've inside the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN, is called the Senior Service as Britain's oldest armed service

explanation.surface: A rift has been detected within the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Senior Service' is the British Royal Navy, the oldest of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean torn apart; the answer is an old past participle of rive, to tear.

clue.text: Pint-size sergeant major everybody put on

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major
everybody means all

explanation.surface: A tiny sergeant major whom everyone teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' sounds like teasing or a con; in a down clue it means SM sits on top of ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pint-size means tiny, a diminutive measure of build.

clue.text: Gets one's own back

parts.note: read literally as recovering one's own property rather than taking revenge

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means 'takes revenge'; read literally it means recovering what one lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover what one had lost is literally to get one's own back.

clue.text: Tirade interrupted by a politician up in arms?

indicators.note: the tirade synonym is broken open by the next pieces

parts.note: a tirade is a rant
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An angry speech is cut into by a politician who is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' means angry, but the question mark points to heraldry, where a beast rearing up on a coat of arms is so described.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a lion rearing on its hind legs on a coat of arms is described this way, and the word also means rife or unrestrained.

clue.text: Owls that remain silent when there's a

annotationWithheld.why: Owls that remain silent when there's a (7): clue is cut short after 'a', and a search found no fuller print
annotationWithheld.clue: Owls that remain silent when there's a

clue.text: Act of betrayal that fills the theatre

definitions.meaning: a treacherous compromise of one's principles or allies
a show for which every ticket has gone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a treacherous compromise and a show with every seat booked.

clue.text: The mantle of sleep is

annotationWithheld.why: The mantle of sleep is (7): PELISSE is an anagram of SLEEP IS but the clue as held has no anagram indicator, so it looks cut short, and a search found no fuller print

clue.text: Some haven to which no-one returns

parts.note: a haven for ships is a port

indicators.note: returns means the letters for no-one are read backwards

parts.note: no gives NO and one gives I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A harbour from which no one ever comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns NO I (no + one) round to give ION after PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A share or part of something is some of it.

clue.text: Tumbledown place I am brought in to manage

indicators.note: brought in says the I-am piece goes inside the manage synonym

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
the speaker, I

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to take charge of a dilapidated property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts I inside RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict, collapsed building is a crumbling wreck.

clue.text: The Cambridge college that's full of Irishmen?

definitions.text: The Cambridge college that's full of Irishmen?

parts.words: The Cambridge college that's full of Irishmen?
parts.note: names a Cambridge college that shares its name with a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A university college packed with Irish students.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a Cambridge college and also a county in the west of Ireland, so it is full of Irish people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cambridge college shares its name with an Irish county, which is naturally full of Irish people.

clue.text: Bribe doesn't include British cheese

indicators.note: the word Bribe leaves out one of its letters, the British abbreviation

explanation.surface: A bribe given without a British cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British cheese' looks like one item, but 'British' is the B removed from BRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French dairy product from the region east of Paris is a classic cheese.

clue.text: The gambling centre 13 transformed

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of that answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, the tyrant emperor

explanation.surface: A casino city is a changed version of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points to the answer of 13 across; 'transformed' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famed for its casinos and gaming.

clue.text: Marginal plea for restitution of character

definitions.text: Marginal plea for restitution of character

parts.words: Marginal plea for restitution of character
parts.note: a proofreader's note in the margin asking that deleted characters be put back

explanation.surface: A half-hearted request to restore someone's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marginal' and 'character' suggest a weak plea about reputation; it is a proof mark in the margin asking for deleted letters to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write this Latin word ('let it stand') in the margin to cancel a deletion and restore the letters.

clue.text: You may be sure an infallible idle person will

definitions.meaning: someone who never errs and also does nothing commits no errors

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an assurance ('rest assured'), and literally someone who never errs commits no blunders.

clue.text: In luck at coming into a large sum of money

indicators.note: coming into says at is inserted into the money synonym

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money

explanation.surface: Lucky at inheriting a lot of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming into' reads as inheriting money, but it puts AT inside FORTUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lucky and being blessed by chance are synonyms.
